subject: Weekahead: Early asks & QBR runbook
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai, Amira Patel <amira.patel@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2027-04-30T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Weekahead: Early asks & QBR runbook

Team — quick weekahead from my side ahead of QBR rehearsals (two asks at the bottom). I kept this tight so we can forward into the deck.

Wins (anchor points)
- Nimbus POC running in production for 2 pilot clinics; latency SLOs at 180ms median after last infra tweak.
- Cost per 1k tokens down 18% vs baseline after enabling prefix cache on common prompts (thanks infra).
- Security questionnaire returned with only one open item (data retention window) — our SOC2 export was sufficient.

Immediate risks / flags
- Executive procurement at Nimbus is pushing for a revised commercial SLA ask (99.95 availability) — this will need a short note from infra/ops on feasibility and incremental cost. (See attached SLO-asks.xlsx)
- A large E2E regression test shows tokenization edge-case on older client metadata; impacts one integration path for billing exports. Engineering estimates a patch and deploy in ~3 days.
- QBR narrative needs a crisp customer story; Amira offered a short quote but we need a single slide that connects technical wins to business KPIs (reduction in triage time).

Asks (who/what/by-when)
- Karthik: please draft a one-paragraph feasibility note for 99.95 SLA + rough Delta cost by EOD Tue (I need to include in the commercial playbook).
- Laura: can you confirm the customer quote language and 1–2 metrics (reduction in triage time, projected MRR expansion) by Tue noon?
- Soojin: allocate a 10-minute slot in the QBR run-through for incident / fallback play (we need to show graceful degradation).

Attachments: QBR-Runbook-v2.pdf (run order + slides), model-performance-q2.csv (key perf numbers), SLO-asks.xlsx (requested SLA/availability options).

Irene Choi
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Amira Patel <amira.patel@nimbushealth.com>, procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: 2027-04-30T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Weekahead: Early asks & QBR runbook

Thanks — good framing. A few clarifications: 

- Customer quote: Amira shared this line in the last call: "Redwood reduced triage time by ~22% for our pilot clinics, which materially improved throughput during peak hours." I'll request permission to use it verbatim and ask for a 1-sentence attribution (title + clinic).
- Metrics: I can confirm the 22% triage figure and pull a projected MRR expansion estimate (conservative) — I should have a number by Tue 11:30am.
- For the SLO ask: one angle that helps procurement is an optional credit-based SLA (credits that scale with outage minutes); that avoids changing baseline infra SLAs and is easier to price. If Karthik wants to model both (hard SLA + credit option), that would be ideal.

One other note: the billing export edge-case — I asked the ENG lead for the pilot to drop a short note on impacted customers. If the patch is 3 days, we should include a mitigation slide that calls out timeline and rollback plan.

Laura Bennett
VP, Product & GTM
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-30T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Weekahead: Early asks & QBR runbook

On it — I'll sketch two options by EOD Tue:
1) 99.95 hard SLA: list of infra changes and estimated monthly delta (ballpark).
2) Credit-based SLA: credit schedule + how it maps to repayment/offsets.

Also will flag operational runbooks needed for the fallback play and a short note on how the prefix cache affects cold-starts (so the execs get the cost/lift tradeoff).

Karthik
Head of Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Weekahead: Early asks & QBR runbook

Looping back after a sync with Amira — she confirmed willingness to appear on the QBR slide if we share the final customer-facing slide for legal sign-off. She also asked for a single bulleted fallback commitment (what we will do if latency exceeds X) to include in their procurement pack.

New ask: can product/ops draft the fallback commitment language (one paragraph, customer-facing) and share to me + Amira by Tue 2pm? I will handle legal and attribution sign-off after that.

I'll update the runbook after Karthik's SLA options arrive.

Irene
